checks.after: Bing and I differ in rank and are far apart in our positions; moreover, he and his brothers are close relatives of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.

checks.reason: The favored maternal relatives, rather than the rulers, enjoy exceptional glory and then incur the consequences of elevation beyond their station. The replacement correctly conveys both the 負乘 allusion and love causing harm; 殊世 is not reduced to brief duration.
checks.after: Reading the histories, I see maternal relatives indulged and allowed to wield power and disorder the court: first they enjoy extraordinary glory, then suffer the consequences of holding positions beyond their station. This is what is meant by love proving sufficient to cause harm.

checks.reason: 防萌終寵 pairs prevention of incipient trouble with preservation of favor to the end. Enfeoffment and hereditary succession of the vassal state, illustrated by Qi and Chen under Zhou, are faithfully retained without a frontier-state claim.
checks.after: I have often resented that successive rulers did not fully master the means of preventing incipient trouble while preserving favor to the end. Why not establish these relatives with a territorial fief and let their descendants inherit the vassal state, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?

checks.reason: The replacement retains the modest self-description, the unnamed former emperor as grantor, appointment among the generals, the people of several commanderies, actual fighting, seasonal allocation, unexhausted forces, surplus grain, growing fear and territory, and the contrast with imperial resources. No formal column-command office or emperor identification is imposed.
checks.after: Though deficient in virtue, I undeservedly received appointment as one of the former emperor’s generals. With the people of only several commanderies, I still aspire to engulf powerful enemies. Thus, from recent times until now we have crossed weapons in battle, farming for one season and fighting for three; yet our troops are not exhausted, our granaries have surplus grain, our enemies fear us more each day, and our territory grows daily. How much greater, then, are imperial majesty and its imposing power—how could the two be compared!

checks.reason: 列將 is rendered as appointment among generals, and 同年而語 as an idiom of comparison rather than a year assertion. The remaining military and agricultural propositions and the contrast with sovereign power are preserved; the former emperor remains unnamed.

additionalCorrections.before: Had the altars not been numinous and heaven not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!
additionalCorrections.after: Had the altars not been numinous and men and spirits not aided us, would the hearts of wolves and jackals have been allowed to run their course!
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 人神 names both human and spiritual aid. The existing English substitutes heaven alone and omits the human agents; the correction restores both without changing the hypothetical rhetorical question.

additionalCorrections.before: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his brothers ought to withdraw of their own accord.
additionalCorrections.after: Your Majesty deeply honors family ties; Bing and his fellows ought naturally to look up in expectation.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 引領 means stretching the neck or looking up in expectation, not withdrawing from office. 自宜 does not supply a verb of retirement. The replacement leaves the object of expectation unstated, as in the Chinese.

additionalCorrections.before: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to withdraw.
additionalCorrections.after: Your Majesty deeply honors the ties of Weiyang; Bing and the others ought themselves to stretch their necks in expectation.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The same 引領 error remains in the literal field: the Chinese expresses expectant looking, not withdrawal. The Weiyang kinship expression is retained without adding an unstated object of expectation.

additionalCorrections.before: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in frontier states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
additionalCorrections.after: I have often said: if a ruler wishes to honor maternal kin, enfeoff them in vassal states, enrich their stipends, and limit their power so that the throne shows no partial favor and the realm no private suspicion.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 籓國 denotes the enfeoffed vassal states, not necessarily geographically frontier states. This is the repeated enfeoffment policy also expressed in s0256; only the unsupported frontier characterization is removed.

additionalCorrections.before: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with frontier states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
additionalCorrections.after: Your servant often says: if a ruler of the age wishes to honor the maternal clan, why not enfeoff them with vassal states, enrich their stipends and gifts, and limit their power and advantage, so that above there is no partial favor and below no private talk.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The literal field repeats the unsupported geographical reading of 籓國 as frontier states. Vassal states preserves enfeoffment and agrees with the corrected use at s0256 without asserting location.

additionalCorrections.before: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and name, are far apart in origin and position, and moreover are kin of the state; by reason one ought to yield and rejoice to suit the occasion.
additionalCorrections.after: Your servant and Bing and the others differ in rank and status and are far apart in our situations; moreover, they are close kin of the imperial house. By rights I ought to defer and accommodate myself to the circumstances.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The literal field still leaves the memorialist among the imperial kin, although 又國之戚昵 refers to Bing and his fellows in this contrast. It also treats 降悅 as rejoicing rather than deferential accommodation. The correction makes the kinship owner and the speaker who should defer explicit.

additionalCorrections.before: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of column commanders and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.
additionalCorrections.after: Again he wrote to Bing, saying: You, by the intimacy of the empress's chamber and closeness as maternal kin, hold the pivot in total, issue and receive royal commands, and together hold the posts of generals and provincial overseers; your brothers spread a net, displayed across the capital region.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 列將 occurs again here. Rendering it as column commanders repeats the unsupported office interpretation corrected at s0261 and in claim-440; generals preserves the military positions without importing a column-command title.

additionalCorrections.before: Each time I read the histories, rulers never fail to pamper and indulge the maternal clan, letting them hold power and disorder the court; first they have glory beyond the age, then the burden of riding when unfit, the saying that love rightly becomes harm.
additionalCorrections.after: Whenever I read the histories, I see maternal relatives invariably pampered and indulged, allowed to hold power and disorder the court; first they enjoy glory surpassing their age, then incur the burden of riding when unfit; this is what is meant by love being sufficient to cause harm.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The literal field still makes rulers the explicit subject before the ambiguous they, obscuring the maternal relatives as recipients of glory and calamity. 愛之適足以為害 means love suffices to cause harm, not that love rightly becomes harm. Both substantive problems are corrected while retaining the 負乘 image.

additionalCorrections.before: I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing the first sprout and ending favor; why not grant a single fief and let frontier states succeed one another, as Qi and Chen of Zhou?
additionalCorrections.after: I often resent that rulers of successive ages did not fully use the art of preventing incipient trouble and preserving favor to the end; why not establish them with a territorial fief and let the vassal states be inherited in succession, as with Qi and Chen under Zhou?
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 終寵 means sustaining favor to its end, not ending favor. 令籓國相承 concerns hereditary succession in the enfeoffed states, not frontier states replacing one another. These definite errors remain in the literal field despite correction of the en field.

additionalCorrections.before: Worthy men rallied to them; though eunuchs endangered them and the realm mourned, they could still walk without pride and gave their lives for the state.
additionalCorrections.after: Worthy men rallied to them; although eunuchs brought them into peril, the realm lamented them because they could nonetheless conduct themselves without arrogance and gave their lives for the state.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 故也 makes their unarrogant conduct and service at the cost of their lives the explanation for the realm lamenting them despite the eunuchs bringing them into peril. The existing wording loses this causal relation and reads 履 as physical walking.

additionalCorrections.before: Worthy men gave them their hearts; though endangered by eunuch minions and mourned by the realm, they could still walk without pride and plotted for the state even at the cost of their lives.
additionalCorrections.after: Worthy men gave them their hearts; although they were endangered by eunuch minions, the realm lamented them, because they were still able to conduct themselves without arrogance and took thought for the state at the cost of their lives.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: The literal field also omits the explanatory force of 故也 and turns conduct expressed by 履 into walking. The correction attaches the explanation to the realm lamenting them and retains the supplied Chinese without conjecturally replacing its unusual wording.

additionalCorrections.before: Bing seeing the memorial and letter was greatly afraid; because they were extremely distant, not what they could control; thereupon with He Chong and others memorialized to permit Huang to style King of Yan.
additionalCorrections.after: Bing, seeing the memorial and letter, was greatly afraid; because Huang was extremely far away and beyond his power to control, he thereupon, with He Chong and the others, memorialized to permit Huang to style himself King of Yan.
additionalCorrections.sourceReason: 其絕遠 refers to Huang, the distant person whom Bing cannot control, not to the memorial and letter or to a plural they. The correction restores the pronoun owner and the reflexive force of 皝稱燕王 without changing the event or introducing a date.
